_meta.indication: Treatment of patients 18 years of age and older with complicated urinary tract infections (cUTI) including pyelonephritis, caused by susceptible microorganisms: Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Proteus mirabilis, and Enterobacter cloacae complex.

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Trial AT-301 (also referred to as Trial 1)
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, multicenter, active-controlled noninferiority trial; subjects randomized 1:1 to cefepime-enmetazobactam versus piperacillin/tazobactam.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults 18 years of age and older with complicated urinary tract infections (cUTI) or acute pyelonephritis (AP) requiring hospitalization.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Overall success (composite of clinical cure and microbiologic eradication) at the Test of Cure visit in the microbiological-MITT (m-MITT) population, prespecified noninferiority margin of -10%.
pivotal_trials.n: 1,041 subjects randomized (MITT/safety population 1,034; m-MITT population N=345 cefepime-enmetazobactam and N=333 piperacillin/tazobactam)
pivotal_trials.result: Overall success at Test of Cure occurred in 79.1% (273/345) of the cefepime-enmetazobactam group versus 58.9% (196/333) of the piperacillin/tazobactam group; treatment difference 21.2% (95% CI 14.3, 27.9). Because the lower limit of the 95% CI (14.3%) was above zero and above the prespecified noninferiority margin of -10%, the trial demonstrated both noninferiority and superiority of cefepime-enmetazobactam over piperacillin/tazobactam.

key_safety: Most frequently reported adverse reactions (≥5%) were transaminases increased (20% vs 20%), bilirubin increased (7% vs 4%), headache (5% vs 2%), and phlebitis/infusion site reactions (5% vs <1%). Treatment was discontinued due to adverse reactions in 3% (13/516) of EXBLIFEP patients versus 2% (10/518) of piperacillin/tazobactam patients. Warnings include hypersensitivity reactions, neurotoxicity, and C. difficile-associated diarrhea.
target_moa: Cefepime is a cephalosporin whose bactericidal action results from inhibition of bacterial cell wall synthesis by binding penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs); enmetazobactam is a beta-lactamase inhibitor that protects cefepime from degradation by certain serine beta-lactamases such as ESBL.
modality: Small molecule combination product: cefepime (a cephalosporin beta-lactam antibacterial) and enmetazobactam (a beta-lactamase inhibitor) for injection.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; outside expertise was not necessary as there were no controversial issues that would benefit from advisory committee discussion.

summary.text: NDA 216165 was submitted June 22, 2023 with both Fast Track and Qualified Infectious Disease Product (QIDP) designations; the sponsor requested and was granted priority review, with a PDUFA goal date of February 22, 2024. Approval was based on a single Phase 3 noninferiority trial (AT-301) and was not an accelerated approval.

citations.quote: Allecra Therapeutics SAS, submitted NDA 216165 for cefepime-enmetazobactam for injection, for the treatment of cUTI, including pyelonephritis, on June 22, 2023. The NDA has both Fast Track and Qualified Infectious Disease Product designations. Allecra requested priority NDA review.
The NDA was filed on August 21, 2023, and granted a priority review. The Prescription Drug User Fee Act goal date for NDA 216165 is February 22, 2024.
The Applicant submitted a single phase 3, randomized, assessor-blinded, active-controlled noninferiority trial in 1,034 hospitalized adults with cUTI and AP.

requirement.text: 4582-1 Conduct an open-label, single arm, non-comparative study to evaluate the pharmacokinetics, safety and tolerability of multiple doses of cefepime/enmetazobactam in pediatric patients from birth to less than 18 years of age with complicated urinary tract infections, including pyelonephritis.

requirement.text: 4582-2 Conduct a US surveillance study over a five-year period after the introduction of cefepime/enmetazobactam to the market to determine if bacterial resistance or decreased susceptibility to cefepime/enmetazobactam is occurring in the target population of bacteria that are in the approved cefepime/enmetazobactam label.
